full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff-appellants filed the suit for declaration of tittle. The plaintiffs alleged that the land described in schedules A and B to the plaint belonged in Khash to Dhaka Nawab Court of Ward Estate. Subsequently the plaintiffs took settlement of the lands of schedule A and B for salami of Taka 2,273.50 paisa and Taka 4,057.50 paisa respectively in the year 1353 BS after fulfilling all the formalities required by the estate. The plaintiffs were in possession of the lands of both the schedules openly and adversely against all others since the year 1353 BS. The plaintiffs by different kabalas sold out all other lands except the lands described in schedule C to the plaint. Now the plaintiffs are in possession of the C Schedule land which formed the subject matter of the suit. The men of defendant i.e. the Government have set up clam to the C schedule land as forest land and sought to posses the same in spite of the fact that the Government never acquired the said land which bear no forests and to which the plaintiffs had acquired indefeasible title by virtue of lease and possession for more than 25 years. Illegal claim set up by the Government-defendant had cast a cloud upon the title of the plaintiffs giving cause of action for the suit. 

 3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit land as well as A and B schedule lands were forest land in the khas possession of the Dhaka Nawab court of ward Estate. All the forest land under Nawab Estate within the suit village Choota Kaliakor PS Savar were acquired under East Bengal Private Forest Land and accordingly the Collector, Dhaka invited application from the public under section of the Act to put forward their claim for the land if any, and the same was published in Dhaka Gazette dated 6th May, 1994. None including the plaintiffs put forward their claim within the specified time and consequently CS Plot Nos. 11,14, 22, 32, 88, 129, 138, 161, 170, 171, 189 and 191 of the said mouza comprising an area of 137.34 acres of land were decided to be constituted as a reserve forest. A notification to that effect bearing No. 3125 was published in the Dhaka Gazette dated 13th April, 1955 and since then the suit land and the other lands of the aforesaid plots constitute a reserve forest in possession of the forest department of the Government. It is further contended by the defendant that the plaintiff's story of lease from the Dhaka Nawab Court of ward Estate is absolutely false. The plaintiffs had fabricated some false documents in collaboration with the officials of the Court of Ward Estate and they had no possession of the suit land. The suit was therefore, liable to be dismissed.
